paths.description: Anonymous home/listing template and global chrome; first-load consent, preferences, responsive layout, security, network, accessibility, discoverability, and memory.
Trending section listing archetype representing catalogue collection pages.
Album/detail archetype and primary anonymous play journey after rejecting consent.

findings.summary: Theme is fixed dark instead of following the user’s colour-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: Dark and default screenshots are byte-identical (480,889 bytes), and the CSS probe found zero prefers-color-scheme, color-scheme, or light-dark() uses.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven light/dark tokens with light-dark() or prefers-color-scheme.

findings.summary: Reduced-motion preference does not suppress non-essential motion.
findings.evidence: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, the probe still found 34 running animations and transitions up to 1s; CSS inspection found no reduced-motion media query.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a prefers-reduced-motion: reduce override that removes decorative animation and shortens non-essential transitions.

findings.summary: State and route changes do not use View Transitions.
findings.evidence: The CSS platform probe found zero view-transition rules; the album play video shows an abrupt state update rather than a spatial transition.
findings.suggestedFix: Use same-document View Transitions for route and major state changes, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: The consent banner obscures core content on every first load.
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshots show the banner covering roughly the lower third; at 360x800 it consumes nearly the entire viewport and hides the player.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the large first-load interruption with a compact, content-preserving consent surface while keeping accept and reject equally easy.

findings.summary: The consent overlay is custom chrome rather than a semantic modal primitive.
findings.evidence: DOM recon found zero dialog, popover, or details elements while the screenshot shows a modal-like consent surface.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a native dialog for the consent decision, with focus trapping, Escape handling where policy permits, and an explicit accessible name.

findings.summary: The first-load experience overflows by 441px on a 360px viewport.
findings.evidence: Layout measured scrollWidth/innerWidth 801px against a 360px visual viewport on both home and album; the mobile screenshot clips the consent actions off-screen.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the 801px minimum layout from the consent surface, allow controls and text to wrap, and verify at 320–400px and zoomed conditions.

findings.summary: The consent component does not adapt to its available container.
findings.evidence: The same 801px consent layout is retained in a 360px visual viewport, and CSS inspection found no container queries.
findings.suggestedFix: Make the consent component intrinsically fluid and add a container query to stack actions and constrain copy at narrow inline sizes.

findings.summary: Many controls have undersized hit areas and focus indication is unclear.
findings.evidence: The active probe found numerous 17–22px-tall links and computed outlines with style none for sampled controls; 210 focusable elements create a dense keyboard path.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide at least 24x24 CSS px targets (prefer 44x44 for primary touch controls) and a strong :focus-visible ring.

findings.summary: Load performance and visual stability are far outside good ranges.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 25.4s and CLS 0.434; the independent mobile layout observer measured CLS 0.242.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the LCP dependency chain, prioritize the actual LCP resource, reserve late content space, and defer non-critical scripts.

findings.summary: Late-loading UI causes substantial layout shift.
findings.evidence: The mobile layout observer recorded seven shifts totalling 0.242, including a single 0.144 shift; all 56 inspected images lacked width/height attributes.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve dimensions or aspect-ratio for imagery and the consent/player regions, and use stable font fallbacks.

findings.summary: The main thread is blocked by long tasks.
findings.evidence: Trace summary recorded seven long tasks, a 340ms longest task, and 504ms total blocking time.
findings.suggestedFix: Break up long tasks, schedule non-urgent work by priority, and delay analytics/recaptcha until user intent requires them.

findings.summary: Critical delivery is heavy and delays visible content.
findings.evidence: HAR captured 167 requests and 4.77MB transferred, including 2.50MB script and 0.96MB font; the main web-player bundle alone was 1.08MB.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce the critical dependency chain, subset/dedupe fonts, split the player bundle, and defer consent/analytics dependencies.

findings.summary: Large amounts of unused JS and CSS ship on first load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 630KiB unused JavaScript and 68KiB unused CSS, including 76% waste in the mobile player bundle.
findings.suggestedFix: Code-split by route and capability, conditionally load recaptcha/consent tooling, and remove unused CSS from the initial route.

findings.summary: Heading hierarchy and keyboard focus presentation need correction.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found an H4 “Company” heading that skips levels; the focus probe returned outline style none on sampled controls and a 210-element tab sequence.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a sequential heading outline and define an unmistakable :focus-visible style while pruning nonessential tab stops.

findings.summary: The page cannot reflow at a narrow viewport and declares maximum-scale=1.
findings.evidence: The rendered DOM declares maximum-scale=1, while 360px layout evidence overflows by 441px and clips consent actions.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove maximum-scale=1, fix narrow reflow, and enlarge small interactive targets.

findings.summary: The page logs an uncaught React runtime error.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse captured minified React error #421 from vendor~mobile-web-player.a51ad297.js.
findings.suggestedFix: Resolve the server/client render mismatch that triggers React #421 and add production monitoring that fails builds on uncaught errors.

findings.summary: Image asset markup does not reserve dimensions or offer responsive candidates.
findings.evidence: The image primitive found 56/56 images without width/height, 54 without srcset, and 13 oversized by its 2x display threshold.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit width/height or aspect-ratio and srcset/sizes for artwork variants; keep decorative images explicitly empty-alt.

findings.summary: One consent link uses generic link text.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse identified “More information” as non-descriptive, although anchors and robots are otherwise crawlable.
findings.suggestedFix: Give the link a destination-specific accessible name such as “Learn how cookie consent works”.

findings.summary: Security headers and cookie flags are weaker than the app’s risk profile warrants.
findings.evidence: CSP permits unsafe-eval; Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy are absent; OptanonConsent is not Secure and three cookies use SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove unsafe-eval where feasible, set strict Referrer/Permissions policies, and mark every HTTPS cookie Secure with the narrowest SameSite mode.

findings.summary: The anonymous landing page has a broad third-party and tracking footprint.
findings.evidence: Tracker evidence found 18 third-party origins and known Sentry/GTM trackers; HAR attributed 164/167 requests and 4.76MB to non-main origins.
findings.suggestedFix: Minimize pre-consent requests, self-host or delay nonessential dependencies, and batch strictly necessary analytics after consent.

findings.summary: Defensive browser policies are incomplete.
findings.evidence: Headers evidence found no Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy and a CSP weakened by unsafe-eval; frame-ancestors and HSTS are present.
findings.suggestedFix: Add restrictive Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy, remove unsafe-eval, and evaluate Trusted Types for the React application.

findings.summary: Most catalogue content disappears without JavaScript.
findings.evidence: Discoverability measured only 36% raw/rendered content coverage; the crawler screenshot is blank despite a 200 response.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render meaningful listing/detail content and real links, then hydrate playback and personalization progressively.

findings.summary: The consent runtime state is cut off on narrow screens.
findings.evidence: At 360px the consent controls extend 441px beyond the visual viewport, preventing reliable access to all choices.
findings.suggestedFix: Use intrinsic sizing and a narrow-container layout for the consent state; keep all actions visible and keyboard reachable.

findings.summary: The main web player relies heavily on physical left/right CSS.
findings.evidence: The page correctly declares lang=en-GB and dir=ltr, but the CSS probe found 163 physical margin/padding declarations and zero logical-property declarations in accessible stylesheets.
findings.suggestedFix: Migrate layout spacing and positioning to logical inline/block properties and test an RTL locale.

findings.summary: Artwork and fonts are not delivered at an efficient responsive budget.
findings.evidence: Image evidence found 54/56 images without responsive sources and 13 oversized; HAR transferred 0.84MB images and 0.96MB fonts.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve responsive modern artwork variants, subset fonts, and avoid duplicate variable/title font payloads.

findings.summary: The first load performs substantial avoidable work.
findings.evidence: The page transfers 2.50MB of scripts, Lighthouse estimates 630KiB unused JS, and the trace records 504ms blocking time before a user plays anything.
findings.suggestedFix: Deprioritize background work and conditionally load analytics, recaptcha, cast, and player capabilities when needed.

findings.summary: Third-party code dominates the initial resource budget.
findings.evidence: HAR classified 164/167 requests and 4.76MB as outside the main origin, with recaptcha, GTM, and consent tooling among the largest scripts.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party performance budget, delay nonessential tags until consent/intent, and consolidate Spotify-owned CDN delivery accounting.
